body.p: Applicant has thoroughly reviewed the outstanding Office Action dated August 16, 2023, and this reply is believed to be fully responsive thereto. Claims 2-20 are pending, with claim 2 being independent. Claim 1 has been cancelled. Claim 2 is amended. Claims 15-20 are new. No new subject matter has been added. Applicant respectfully requests that all claims be allowed and this application pass to issuance in view of the following remarks.
The title stands objected for allegedly having a typographical error. The title is amended herein as suggested by the Examiner. Withdrawal of this objection is therefore respectfully requested.

Claims 2-7, 9-10 and 13-14 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 102(a)(1)/(a)(2) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2009/0005675 (hereinafter "Grunwald"). Without conceding to the propriety of this rejection, but rather to expedite prosecution, independent claim 2 is amended to recite "a sensor disposed on the distal end of the stylet and configured to detect and measure a physiological parameter in a patient's vasculature" and "wherein a distal portion of the stylet is more flexible than a proximal portion of the stylet." Grunwald fails to disclose or suggest each and every feature recited in amended independent claim 2. Grunwald therefore does not anticipate independent claim 2 or any claims depending therefrom. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection is respectfully requested.

Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Grunwald in view of U.S. Publication No. 2015/0173829 (hereinafter "Lichtenstein"). Claims 11-12 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Grunwald. None of the cited references make up for the aforementioned deficiencies of Grunwald discussed above. Accordingly, a prima facie case of obviousness cannot be established. Reconsideration and withdrawal of these rejections is therefore respectfully requested.

New claims 15-20 depend either directly or indirectly from independent claim 1. At least for the reason of that dependency and the reasons noted above with respect to independent claim 1, Applicant respectfully submits that new claims 15-20 are allowable. Because claims 15-20 recite additional features, however, the individual consideration thereof on their own merits is respectfully requested.
In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant submits that all claims are in condition for allowance, and an indication of such is earnestly solicited.

It is believed that all of the pending issues have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific rejection, issue or comment does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above may not be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Further, Applicants declare

that any amendments herein that are not specifically made for the purpose of patentability are made for other purposes, such as clarification, and that no such changes shall be construed as limiting the scope of the claims or the application of the Doctrine of Equivalents. Finally, nothing in this reply should be construed as an intent to concede any issue with regard to any claim, except as specifically stated in this reply, and the amendment of any claim does not necessarily signify concession of unpatentability of the claim prior to its amendment.

It would be appreciated if the Examiner would telephone the undersigned attorney at 202-861-1500 concerning any questions related to this response in an effort to resolve any matter sill outstanding before issuing another action.

The fees due in connection with a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) are being submitted concurrently with the filing of this paper on the Electronic Filing System (EFS). In the event that any charges or credits are due in connection with this filing or otherwise, however, please apply any such charges or credits to Deposit Account 50-2036 with reference to Atty. Docket No. 40792.24546.
Respectfully submitted, BAKER & HOSTETLER LLP/Jonathan S. Werner/
